subtitle: AREA MAN BANNED FOR 24 HOURS FROM TEAMSPEAK FOR BEING 20 SECONDS LATE FROM THE BATHROOM THE CHANGE NAME
changed the title so people would look haha
Ayo, lads.
So, in another spectacular showing at the theater of the Avicus Teamspeak, our dear friend Spartemex was harassing me yet again about my teamspeak username. I suppose it's because I don't even come close to breaking any other (and/or important) rules and so that's the only thing he can try to get me on, despite the fact that I've been following the Teamspeak rules to the letter. Anyways, at this point you may be wondering why such a kind and caring individual would come after an honest citizen like I, and for those of you who do not know, I shall spell out the events of the past week or so that occurred between myself, Spartemex, and several of my associates. 

It all started on a relatively sunny day, at least where I live. The date was March 4th, 2017. The time was around 2:30 pm Pacific. I was participating in a relatively-well publicized map testing event, along with the rest of my team. It was an 8v8, against Horizon, on the map "Powerhouse", by Fouled. I have retrieved the chat logs from that match, and I'll let them speak for themselves. Particularly important events have been bolded, at the author's discretion.

Anyways, the gist of it is that Spartemex pretty much completely ballsed up the match by joining in the middle of it. What's not seen in the chatlog is that in response to Spartemex joining and unbalancing the teams, one of our players left (JamesMaxwell), and we were unable to get him back quick enough so we ended up taking an 8v7 until the end of the match. Now that we know what happened, it's time to consider some of the facts:
  • The map testing event was on Community01, which must be joined using /sv community01 and isn't visible on the website or server change majigger
  • It's difficult to tell exactly when Spartemex first came onto the map testing server or when he first joined the match, however you may notice that there's roughly 4 minutes between him saying "Hi" (14:30:25) and his first death (14:33:38). One can only assume that during that time, he'd have been able to observe what was going on in the server quite well
  • The match was an 8v8, on a tournament-size map that hasn't really been played before
  • The team names in the match were "Team Rocket" and "Horizon", which would appear in chat any time someone captured a point and presumably in the tab menu as well.
Despite all of this, Spartemex joined anyway, got 0 kills and 4 deaths, and ALM (pbuh) was forced to ban him to get him to leave the match. I will leave judgment of the situation to the reader, but before I do, I would like to contribute this quotation from the map event:

[13:18:27] [Client thread/INFO]: [CHAT] «OFFICIAL | _Nathy?» "everyones just joining, are they retarded?" - Tazz 2k17

For this "incident", myself and my team gave Spartemex quite a bit of grief, and rightfully so I believe, considering the sheer magnitude of the error and the fact that it was completely out of our control and directly contributed to our loss in the scrim. You may be thinking  "man it's just a scrim blah blah blah", but this was the first time we'd scrimmed in quite a while, as well as our first scrim against Horizon, and our defeat at their hands (with the help of Spartemex) shamed us greatly. At Team Rocket, we take our honor very seriously, and this event was no exception.

At this point you may be wondering what this has to do with my Teamspeak ban. The fact of the matter is that following the "incident" at the map testing event, Spartemex, perhaps in retaliation for some of the angry words we hurled his way after what he did caused our loss in the map testing event, has been undertaking a systematic campaign of harassment against myself and my team members. The primary venue for said harassment has been the Avicus Teamspeak, which is pretty much the only place I've ever seen him (other than the map testing event, of course). Since I don't really break any other rules, for his ammunition he uses the rule regarding usernames. I would quote it here directly but tragically I don't have access to it at the moment. 

In any case, the username I was using at the time (March 11th) was "@ПРОФБАНАНАСЛЭГ (winXP)", which anyone who can read Cyrillic can confirm is simply my username directly transliterated into Cyrillic. If I recall the Teamspeak rules correctly, the rule is merely that your username must be your IGN, and nothing about what alphabet it's in. The night prior even, I had shadowolfyt tell me to change my Teamspeak name, but after I told him it was merely my username in Cyrillic he let me off. Additionally, PieZ removed my media rank that same day and not a peep was heard out of him, either. But, the next day, Spartemex (with me in his sights), refused to let up and listen to the glorious light of reason as I poked him endlessly and even did him the great honor of appearing in his Teamspeak channel in person to argue my point. As a man of honor, I held my righteous ground and refused to change my completely rule-abiding username, and as a result he banned me for like an hour or two, I don't really remember which one it was. What's funny to me is that in the past, I'd gone usernames such as "dr. gerald ya-ya" and the equivalent in Cyrillic for around a month, even showing up to the Senior Q&A with it and not hearing a single peep out of anyone for the entire time I used it. Suddenly, though, I'm using a completely rule-abiding username and a certain mod comes after me. Coincidence? I think not.

This brings me up to the current day, March 13th. Taking Spartemex's "advice" for changing my username, I changed it to "ⓑⓐⓝ (winⓜⓔ)", with the "ban" coming from "profbananaslug", and with "winXP" changed to "winME", referring of course to Windows Millenium Edition, which came out directly preceding Windows XP. This username lasted me through all of yesterday, and quite a bit of today up until 16:50:29. Of course, as usual (noticing a pattern here?), that was not good enough for Spartemex, and after a bit of arguing I was issued an ultimatum: 1 minute to change my username. This is when I began to panic: I only had 1 minute to come up with a clever username that would also sate Spartemex's insatiable appetite for harassing me about my usernames and I also had to take a really big honkin' piss. You see, I had only recently returned from my classes at school, where I do not use the "facilities" so-to-speak because of their general lack of cleanliness. My drink of choice also happens to be iced tea, and caffeine consumption generally leads to increased urine output, and of course as it tends to happen, I was only overwhelmed by the need to take a piss at the worst possible time. Quickly, I stammered out (typing slow because I kept making mistakes in my haste) a message requesting an extension. Unfortunately, my bias for whole numbers won out yet again, and instead of asking for a decent amount of time that would allow me to do everything I had to, I instead asked for an extension until 4:50, which gave me barely two minutes. Then, in my infinite wisdom I decided to comment on Spartemex's strictness with all the ultimatums and time limits and whatnot, and then I realized that he might've misinterpreted it so I had to send some more messages for clarification. Then, as fast as a possibly could, I dashed out of the room and ran for the closest bathroom, where I squeezed my bladder harder than I squeezed the nurse's hand during my ass surgery when they were injecting me with copious amounts of lidocaine. I will admit that I did not wash my hands on my way out, instead sprinting out of the room as fast as I could to get back to my computer. Unfortunately, I was too late, and the message stared at me mockingly from my screen, stating that I'd been banned. Here's a chatlog of those last fateful minutes:

<16:47:38> "Spartemex" pokes you: Didn't want it to come to this, but change your name to something with "prof" within the next minute
<16:47:47> "Spartemex" pokes you: or I will ban you for another day
<16:48:06> You poked "Spartemex" with message: sec
<16:48:20> You poked "Spartemex" with message: going to the bathroom just gimme until the goddamn 50
<16:48:33> You poked "Spartemex" with message: that's two minutes but then again can't get away with nothing
<16:48:40> "Spartemex" pokes you: Go for it
<16:48:49> You poked "Spartemex" with message: they ought to call you the iron lady like margaret thatcher
<16:48:54> "Crazy_" connected to channel "Main Lobby"
<16:48:57> "Crazy_" switched from channel "Main Lobby" to "Chat #5: Cursing Allowed"
<16:48:57> Channel group "Guest" was assigned to "Crazy_" by "Avicus :: TeamSpeak".
<16:48:58> You poked "Spartemex" with message: former pm of great britain
<16:49:02> "enr1" switched from channel "Chat #8: Spanish Chat (No Maldecir)" to "Chat #5: Cursing Allowed"
<16:49:02> Channel group "Guest" was assigned to "enr1" by "Avicus :: TeamSpeak".
<16:50:29> You were banned for 1 day from the server by "Spartemex" (Refusing to follow change name after repeated requests.)
<16:50:29> Disconnected from server

In conclusion, as you can plainly see from this post, I was merely a victim of circumstance and overly-harsh/treacherous mods, and if there remains but a single spark of Justice left alive in the Universe, I humbly beg that you bless me with it and overturn this preposterous ban.

Veritas omnia vincit.






I don't know if they've changed this, but it's impossible for the OP to reply in Teamspeak appeals. If you want to continue the discussion with me, feel free to hit me up on Teamspeak send an e-mail to me at theasicisreal@profbananaslug.net.

Ayo, lads.
So, in another spectacular showing at the theater of the Avicus Teamspeak, our dear friend Spartemex was harassing me yet again about my teamspeak username. I suppose it's because I don't even come close to breaking any other (and/or important) rules and so that's the only thing he can try to get me on, despite the fact that I've been following the Teamspeak rules to the letter. Anyways, at this point you may be wondering why such a kind and caring individual would come after an honest citizen like I, and for those of you who do not know, I shall spell out the events of the past week or so that occurred between myself, Spartemex, and several of my associates. 

It all started on a relatively sunny day, at least where I live. The date was March 4th, 2017. The time was around 2:30 pm Pacific. I was participating in a relatively-well publicized map testing event, along with the rest of my team. It was an 8v8, against Horizon, on the map "Powerhouse", by Fouled. Anyways, the gist of it is that Spartemex pretty much completely ballsed up the match by joining in the middle of it. What's not seen in the chatlog is that in response to Spartemex joining and unbalancing the teams, one of our players left (JamesMaxwell), and we were unable to get him back quick enough so we ended up taking an 8v7 until the end of the match. Now that we know what happened, it's time to consider some of the facts:
  • The map testing event was on Community01, which must be joined using /sv community01 and isn't visible on the website or server change majigger
  • It's difficult to tell exactly when Spartemex first came onto the map testing server or when he first joined the match, however you may notice that there's roughly 4 minutes between him saying "Hi" (14:30:25) and his first death (14:33:38). One can only assume that during that time, he'd have been able to observe what was going on in the server quite well
  • The match was an 8v8, on a tournament-size map that hasn't really been played before
  • The team names in the match were "Team Rocket" and "Horizon", which would appear in chat any time someone captured a point and presumably in the tab menu as well.
Despite all of this, Spartemex joined anyway, got 0 kills and 4 deaths, and ALM (pbuh) was forced to ban him to get him to leave the match. I will leave judgment of the situation to the reader, but before I do, I would like to contribute this quotation from the map event:

[13:18:27] [Client thread/INFO]: [CHAT] «OFFICIAL | _Nathy?» "everyones just joining, are they retarded?" - Tazz 2k17

For this "incident", myself and my team gave Spartemex quite a bit of grief, and rightfully so I believe, considering the sheer magnitude of the error and the fact that it was completely out of our control and directly contributed to our loss in the scrim. You may be thinking  "man it's just a scrim blah blah blah", but this was the first time we'd scrimmed in quite a while, as well as our first scrim against Horizon, and our defeat at their hands (with the help of Spartemex) shamed us greatly. At Team Rocket, we take our honor very seriously, and this event was no exception.

At this point you may be wondering what this has to do with my Teamspeak ban. The fact of the matter is that following the "incident" at the map testing event, Spartemex, perhaps in retaliation for some of the angry words we hurled his way after what he did caused our loss in the map testing event, has been undertaking a systematic campaign of harassment against myself and my team members. The primary venue for said harassment has been the Avicus Teamspeak, which is pretty much the only place I've ever seen him (other than the map testing event, of course). Since I don't really break any other rules, for his ammunition he uses the rule regarding usernames. I would quote it here directly but tragically I don't have access to it at the moment. 

In any case, the username I was using at the time (March 11th) was "@ПРОФБАНАНАСЛЭГ (winXP)", which anyone who can read Cyrillic can confirm is simply my username directly transliterated into Cyrillic. If I recall the Teamspeak rules correctly, the rule is merely that your username must be your IGN, and nothing about what alphabet it's in. The night prior even, I had shadowolfyt tell me to change my Teamspeak name, but after I told him it was merely my username in Cyrillic he let me off. Additionally, PieZ removed my media rank that same day and not a peep was heard out of him, either. But, the next day, Spartemex (with me in his sights), refused to let up and listen to the glorious light of reason as I poked him endlessly and even did him the great honor of appearing in his Teamspeak channel in person to argue my point. As a man of honor, I held my righteous ground and refused to change my completely rule-abiding username, and as a result he banned me for like an hour or two, I don't really remember which one it was. What's funny to me is that in the past, I'd gone usernames such as "dr. gerald ya-ya" and the equivalent in Cyrillic for around a month, even showing up to the Senior Q&A with it and not hearing a single peep out of anyone for the entire time I used it. Suddenly, though, I'm using a completely rule-abiding username and a certain mod comes after me. Coincidence? I think not.

This brings me up to the current day, March 13th. Taking Spartemex's "advice" for changing my username, I changed it to "ⓑⓐⓝ (winⓜⓔ)", with the "ban" coming from "profbananaslug", and with "winXP" changed to "winME", referring of course to Windows Millenium Edition, which came out directly preceding Windows XP. This username lasted me through all of yesterday, and quite a bit of today up until 16:50:29. Of course, as usual (noticing a pattern here?), that was not good enough for Spartemex, and after a bit of arguing I was issued an ultimatum: 1 minute to change my username. This is when I began to panic: I only had 1 minute to come up with a clever username that would also sate Spartemex's insatiable appetite for harassing me about my usernames and I also had to take a really big honkin' piss. You see, I had only recently returned from my classes at school, where I do not use the "facilities" so-to-speak because of their general lack of cleanliness. My drink of choice also happens to be iced tea, and caffeine consumption generally leads to increased urine output, and of course as it tends to happen, I was only overwhelmed by the need to take a piss at the worst possible time. Quickly, I stammered out (typing slow because I kept making mistakes in my haste) a message requesting an extension. Unfortunately, my bias for whole numbers won out yet again, and instead of asking for a decent amount of time that would allow me to do everything I had to, I instead asked for an extension until 4:50, which gave me barely two minutes. Then, in my infinite wisdom I decided to comment on Spartemex's strictness with all the ultimatums and time limits and whatnot, and then I realized that he might've misinterpreted it so I had to send some more messages for clarification. Then, as fast as a possibly could, I dashed out of the room and ran for the closest bathroom, where I squeezed my bladder harder than I squeezed the nurse's hand during my ass surgery when they were injecting me with copious amounts of lidocaine. I will admit that I did not wash my hands on my way out, instead sprinting out of the room as fast as I could to get back to my computer. Unfortunately, I was too late, and the message stared at me mockingly from my screen, stating that I'd been banned. Here's a chatlog of those last fateful minutes:

In conclusion, as you can plainly see from this post, I was merely a victim of circumstance and overly-harsh/treacherous mods, and if there remains but a single spark of Justice left alive in the Universe, I humbly beg that you bless me with it and overturn this preposterous ban.

Veritas omnia vincit.
